claim_verdicts.evidence: "The direction of dependency within the application should be in the direction of abstraction, not implementation details." ... "implementation details can be written to depend on and implement higher-level abstractions, rather than the other way around." Lesson section 3 wording (high-level code depends on an abstraction, not a concrete low-level implementation) matches.

git show stage-1:samples/DonHang.Samples/Samples/Design/OrderNotifications.cs lines 9-23: `private readonly EmailNotifier notifier = new();`, `public sealed class OrderNotifications(INotifier notifier)`, both Handle bodies `notifier.Send(orderId, "order placed")`. Lesson block matches character-for-character.

git show stage-1:DonHang.Domain/OrderService.cs lines 6-23: `OrderService(IOrderRepository repository, INotifier notifier)`, PlaceOrderAsync calls `notifier.Send(order.Id, "order placed")`; no concrete notifier type named anywhere in the file. Lesson block matches.

DonHang.Domain/INotifier.cs: `namespace DonHang.Domain; public interface INotifier { void Send(int orderId, string subject); }`. DonHang.Infrastructure/LoggingNotifier.cs: `public sealed class LoggingNotifier(ILogger<LoggingNotifier> logger) : INotifier` whose Send calls `logger.LogInformation(...)`.

DonHang.Infrastructure.csproj: `<ProjectReference Include="..\DonHang.Domain\DonHang.Domain.csproj" />`. DonHang.Domain.csproj contains only a PropertyGroup: no ProjectReference (and no PackageReference).
"Three situations always produce an implicit reference conversion: ... assigning a reference type instance to a variable of an interface the type implements, ..."

Docs: "The class must provide an implementation for every member declared in the interface" (interfaces.md:35; :86 adds "unless the interface provides a default implementation"). So NotifierBase must change: true. But lesson section 4 goes further: "NotifierBase — and with it EmailNotifier and SmsNotifier — would have to change too". Test: changed Send to (int, string, bool) in INotifier and NotifierBase only, EmailNotifier/SmsNotifier untouched -> `dotnet build`: 0 Warning(s), 0 Error(s).
claim_verdicts.source: refs/dotnet-docs/docs/csharp/fundamentals/types/interfaces.md lines 35, 86; scratch build of stage-1 Samples/Oop/INotifier.cs + NotifierBase.cs
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: The concrete classes depend on `INotifier` too: implementing it means providing every method it declares, so if `Send` changed, `NotifierBase`, which implements it for `EmailNotifier` and `SmsNotifier`, would have to change too.

claim_verdicts.evidence: Checked by inspection of the pattern in the lesson's own code: a class containing `new EmailNotifier()` names EmailNotifier in its source, so it cannot compile without that class and must be edited to use another one, whatever the field type. Consistent with docs: "compile-time dependency flows in the direction of runtime execution" unless the caller depends only on an abstraction.

First half is supported: "The practice of dependency injection is made possible by following the dependency inversion principle" (architectural-principles.md:46), i.e. DI is a separate practice. But "next module" is false: content/path.yaml stage 1 order is design/solid, design/layered, design/dependency-injection; track.yaml also lists module layered between solid and dependency-injection. Injection is two modules later.
claim_verdicts.source: content/path.yaml lines 36-38; content/tracks/design/track.yaml (modules solid, layered, dependency-injection)
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: How the concrete object gets to it — created in one place and passed in — is a separate mechanism, covered later in the dependency-injection module.

issues.text: The sentence says EmailNotifier and SmsNotifier would have to change if Send changed. In this code they only override `Format`; `Send` is declared once, in NotifierBase. Changing Send's parameters in INotifier and NotifierBase, with EmailNotifier/SmsNotifier untouched, builds with 0 errors. The lesson measures change as 'editing the source', so this reads as a false claim.
issues.quote: so if `Send` changed, `NotifierBase` — and with it `EmailNotifier` and `SmsNotifier` — would have to change too
issues.fix: Replace with: "so if `Send` changed, `NotifierBase`, which implements it for `EmailNotifier` and `SmsNotifier`, would have to change too." Keep the next sentence about arrow direction as is.

issues.text: "the subject of the next module" is wrong: path.yaml and track.yaml order stage 1 as design/solid → design/layered → design/dependency-injection. The next module is layered. (depth_notes' "ngay sau" is also inaccurate, but the lesson must follow the real order.)
issues.quote: is a separate mechanism, the subject of the next module
issues.fix: Change to "is a separate mechanism, covered later in the dependency-injection module." Update claim 9 in .meta.json to match.

issues.text: At stage-1 there are two distinct interfaces named INotifier: DonHang.Samples.Oop.INotifier (used by OrderNotifications, implemented by EmailNotifier/SmsNotifier) and DonHang.Domain.INotifier (used by OrderService, implemented by LoggingNotifier). The lesson and summary line 3 speak of 'an INotifier' for both and say OrderService knows 'exactly' what OrderNotifications knows, inviting the reader to think EmailNotifier could be passed to OrderService. It cannot.
issues.fix: After that sentence add: "It is a separate interface from the samples' `INotifier`, with the same single method; `EmailNotifier` and `SmsNotifier` implement the samples one, not this one." (Repo note, not for the lesson: DonHang.Domain/INotifier.cs comment says OrderNotifications depends on it, which is false.)
